Subject: Carrier rationalization & shipping cutover: timeline and SLAs

Hi all,

We're starting the carrier rationalization effort for Redwood's US workplace program: consolidate telecom accounts, standardize laptop shipping logistics for new hires, and lock a cutover window for our January-to-Q2 onboarding surge. High level ask: we need a coordinated plan that covers (1) SIM/carrier porting & number consolidation, (2) bulk laptop shipment SLA for both staged and expedited deliveries, and (3) a dry-run/test cutover in one region.

Attached is a working matrix and a proposed cutover timeline (v2). Please review and call out any hard blockers or assumptions by EOD Thursday. Key constraints from procurement: 30-day PO lead time and invoice terms 30/Net.

Attachments: redwood_carrier_rationalization_matrix.xlsx; shipping_cutover_timeline_v2.xlsx

Next steps I expect:
- Nimbus: feasibility and carrier-level lead times + any porting fees
- ShipFast: SLA for pallet vs individual shipments, expedited rates for onboarding kits
- Claire/Workspace Partners: hotdesk telecom handoff and on-site contact for dry-run

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Head of Workplace Operations
Redwood Inference

1) For the dry-run, do you want us to stand up a temporary hotdesk site or run it entirely from our existing NYC site?
2) Are personal numbers being ported (employees keep numbers) or are we moving to company-managed eSIMs?

We can support on-site coordination and provide a single point of contact (onsite lead) for the cutover day. I'll put together a list of on-site logistics tasks and share by Wednesday morning.

Best,

Logan — appreciate the heads up. Quick responses:

- Porting: typical port-out window is 7–10 business days per block of numbers; bulk port programs can compress this to 4–6 days if we get signed LOAs and authorization templates in advance.
- eSIM vs physical SIM: we support both. eSIM provisioning has a faster activation path for new hires (same-day activation in many cases) but requires device compatibility.
- Costs: porting fees vary; estimate $0.50–$2.00/number depending on carrier. I'll attach a short rate card in my follow-up.

Obstacle to note: if Redwood wants to consolidate billing across three legacy accounts into a single master account, we'll need billing reconciliation data for the last 6 months. Can your procurement team share?

Regards,
Daniel Cho
Enterprise Sales, Nimbus Telecom
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <sales@nimbustel.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>, Claire Roberts <claire@workspacepartners.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Carrier rationalization & shipping cutover: timeline and SLAs

Daniel — we can provide the 6 months of billing exports. I'll upload to the Drive link and share permission. A couple of procurement guardrails:

- PO time: we need to issue a PO 30 calendar days before any paid service change; exceptions require VP approval.
- Payment terms: standard is Net 30; early-pay discounts should be specified in the quote.
- SLAs: any penalty/credit structure needs to be explicit (e.g., failed on-time delivery >2% triggers credits).

Uploading: redwood_billing_6mo_export.csv to drive now.

Monica Patel
Sr. Procurement Manager

Forwarding the thread — ShipFast, we need a firm SLA and a proposed cutover staffing plan for the week of April 18 (preferred) and an alternate window in May. Focus items:
- Bulk staging (pallet -> regional hub -> last-mile)
- Expedited individual shipments (overnight/2-day) for critical hires
- Failure modes & remedial actions (missing unit, damaged, incorrect image)

Also attached: draft_SLA_shipfast.pdf (initial). Please confirm turnaround for the revised SLA and any requirements for packing lists or ASN formats.

Thanks,
Logan
From: ShipFast Ops <ops@shipfast.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Claire Roberts <claire@workspacepartners.com>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Carrier rationalization & shipping cutover: timeline and SLAs

Logan / team — thanks for the context. High-level response and commitments:

- SLA: 98.5% on-time for standard shipments (2-day) and 95% for expedited (overnight) once ASN and manifest templates are standardized. Credits: 5% service credit for monthly on-time below SLA by >1% tier.
- Cutover staffing: we can provide a 2-person on-site coordinator + 1 remote ops lead for cutover week; larger events can be expanded to 4 people.
- Test/dry-run: propose April 12 as a staged dry-run for 150 units in the SF region.
- Packing / ASN: we accept CSV manifests with the following headers: order_id, sku, imei, recipient_name, address, phone, expedite_flag.
- Lead times: pallet to regional hub 2–4 business days; last-mile 1–2 business days after hub.

Attached: draft_SLA_shipfast.pdf (annotated), shipping_cutover_timeline_v2.xlsx (updated with dry-run date).

We'll send a clean SLA and rate sheet by Monday.

— ShipFast Operations
ops@shipfast.com
